newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Japan manufacturers want stable currency.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Japan manufacturers want stable currency.

text.p: U.S. and Japanese manufacturing representatives agreed to tell their governments of the need for a stable currency, a Japanese executive said on Tuesday.

Yuzaburo Mogi, chief executive officer of Kikkoman Corp, said U.S. and Japanese manufacturers meeting in San Francisco had agreed that "we'd better have stability (in the exchange rate). That means not too much up and down."
"But we can't say what rate is appropriate," Mogi told reporters at the U.S.-Japan business conference.
"We agreed we had better tell the necessity of stability of currency to both the Japanese government and the American government," Mogi said.
Mogi was talking about discussions held on Tuesday in the manufacturing group, which met separately from information technology and services industry executives at the conference.

A Japanese executive who attended discussions of the services group said both the U.S. and Japanese delegates in that group would be comfortable with a rate of between 110 yen and 120 yen to the dollar.
Mogi said the U.S.-Japan business conference, which will end on Wednesday, had been "very friendly and productive."

"I think that American society maybe appreciates the efforts of the Japanese people in the field of deregulation of the market. Of course, they are not satisfied yet," Mogi said. "However, they appreciate the effort and the progress."
